description: PowerShell cmdlet to audit Windows Defender Firewall rules for network exposure and security posture.
prerequisites: Admin privileges for full rule visibility

flags.purpose: Lists only active firewall rules currently enforced by Windows Defender Firewall.
flags.security_use_case: Quickly audit which firewall rules are actively allowing or blocking traffic.
flags.threat_detected: Malicious rules added by malware to allow backdoor communication or disable protection.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Large output in environments with many rules.
flags.safe_followup: Review suspicious rules with Get-NetFirewallPortFilter and Get-NetFirewallAddressFilter.

flags.purpose: Filters firewall rules by traffic direction (Inbound or Outbound).
flags.security_use_case: Identify inbound rules that expose services to the network or internet.
flags.threat_detected: Unauthorized inbound access rules created by attackers for persistence.
flags.safe_followup: Cross-check listening ports using Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen.

flags.purpose: Shows rules explicitly allowing traffic through the firewall.
flags.security_use_case: Audit allowed traffic paths that could be abused by malware.
flags.threat_detected: Rules allowing suspicious ports, applications, or remote addresses.
flags.safe_followup: Inspect rule details using Get-NetFirewallApplicationFilter and PortFilter.

flags.purpose: Search firewall rules by human-readable name patterns.
flags.security_use_case: Find rules related to RDP, WinRM, SMB, or other remote access services.
flags.threat_detected: Rogue rules masquerading as legitimate system rules.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Naming can be misleading.
flags.safe_followup: Verify rule origin and associated service or application.

flags.purpose: Filters rules applied to Domain, Private, or Public network profiles.
flags.security_use_case: Detect sensitive services accidentally exposed on Public networks.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Profile detection depends on network configuration.
flags.safe_followup: Restrict rules to Domain/Private using Set-NetFirewallRule if misconfigured.

flags.purpose: Maps firewall rules to specific executable programs.
flags.security_use_case: Identify which applications are allowed through the firewall.
flags.threat_detected: Malware executable granted firewall access for C2 communication.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Requires correlation with application legitimacy.
flags.safe_followup: Check file hash with Get-FileHash and process details with Get-Process.

flags.purpose: Filters rules affecting specific local ports.
flags.security_use_case: Audit exposure of RDP (3389), SMB (445), WinRM (5985).
flags.safe_followup: Verify necessity of open administrative ports.

flags.purpose: Shows rules allowing traffic from external IP ranges.
flags.security_use_case: Detect rules permitting access from any external IP.
flags.threat_detected: Firewall exceptions allowing attacker infrastructure communication.
flags.safe_followup: Restrict rules to specific trusted IP ranges.

powerful_combinations.command: Get-NetFirewallRule -Enabled True -Direction Inbound -Action Allow | Get-NetFirewallPortFilter | Select-Object Name,LocalPort,Protocol
powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Lists all allowed inbound ports through the firewall for quick exposure assessment.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Rapid discovery of services exposed to the network that attackers may target.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Shows all applications explicitly allowed through the firewall.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detecting malware or unknown binaries granted firewall permissions.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Identifies services exposed when connected to public networks like WiFi hotspots.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Preventing accidental exposure of sensitive services outside trusted environments.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Finds rules that allow traffic from any remote address.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detecting overly permissive firewall configurations that attackers exploit.
